_about: Starting points shown in Settings > Connectors > Add connector. Each is an MCP server published by its vendor or the community; check its own documentation for the exact command and the settings it needs. Secrets are written as ${NAME} and stored in .env, never here.

templates.name: slack
templates.title: Slack
templates.description: Read channels and messages, post messages and replies in Slack
templates.secrets_help: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: a Slack app bot token (xoxb-...); SLACK_TEAM_ID: your workspace ID (T...).

templates.name: whatsapp
templates.title: WhatsApp
templates.secrets_help: Pick a WhatsApp MCP server (for example one built on the WhatsApp Business Cloud API or Twilio) and use its command and settings.

templates.name: github
templates.title: GitHub
templates.description: Issues, pull requests and repositories on GitHub
templates.secrets_help: GITHUB_MCP_TOKEN: a GitHub personal access token.

templates.name: files
templates.title: Shared folder
templates.description: Read files in a folder on this computer
templates.secrets_help: SHARED_FOLDER: the folder path, for example C:\Company\Shared.

templates.name: jobs
templates.title: Job board
templates.description: Post jobs and read applicants on a job board that offers an MCP server
templates.secrets_help: Use the MCP URL and token from your job board (for example Indeed, if your account offers MCP access).

templates.name: custom
templates.title: Any MCP server
templates.secrets_help: Any server that speaks MCP over Streamable HTTP (a URL) or stdio (a command).
